summary:
Public Law 118-185, the "Swanson and Hugh Butler Reservoirs Land Conveyances Act" (H.R. 8413, enacted December 23, 2024), authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Commissioner of Reclamation, to convey specified parcels of Federal land at Swanson Reservoir (Trenton Dam) and Hugh Butler Reservoir (Red Willow Dam)—both components of the Pick-Sloan Missouri Basin Program, Frenchman-Cambridge Division, authorized under section 9 of the Flood Control Act of 1944—to Hitchcock County and Frontier County, Nebraska.

Section 2 defines the five conveyable parcels (collectively "requested Federal land"): the Lakeview Lodge Permitted Concession Land, and the Red Willow and Swanson Permitted Cabin Land and Permitted Concession Land, delineated by referenced Bureau of Reclamation maps.

Section 3(a)(1) imposes a deadline of not later than three years after enactment for the Secretary to make good faith efforts to negotiate and enter into "title transfer agreements" conveying all requested United States right, title, and interest. Conveyance conditions include conveyance in whole, a prohibition on subdivision, and a demonstration plan addressing the county's technical/financial capacity and compliance with State fire, safety, and health codes within two years of conveyance. Section 3(a)(2) directs negotiation under the criteria of subtitle A of title VIII of the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (43 U.S.C. 2901 et seq.), notwithstanding section 8002(3)(B) (43 U.S.C. 2902(3)(B)).

Section 3(a)(4) requires consideration equal to fair market value, determined by a Secretary-approved third-party appraiser under USPAP, excluding permit-holder improvements but accounting for foregone future federal revenue streams; disputes resolve under 43 C.F.R. § 2201.4. Payments are "available to the Secretary, subject to further appropriation," for reservoir operations—an authorization, not an appropriation. Counties bear all survey and administrative costs in advance. Section 3(a)(5) restricts post-conveyance use to substantially existing purposes or enumerated recreation/public-purpose, public-access, habitat, or preservation uses.

Section 3(b) bars subsequent reconveyance except at no cost to a Nebraska-recognized public/governmental entity meeting specified adverse-impact, management-capacity, and public-access conditions.

Section 4 subjects conveyances to valid existing rights, Pick-Sloan operational requirements, reserved flowage easements, management-agreement reservations, mineral rights and encumbrances of record as of enactment, elevation-based deed restrictions (2,785 feet at Swanson; 2,628 feet at Hugh Butler), and access easements. It disclaims United States liability for flood damage, requires county indemnification/hold-harmless, preserves Federal Tort Claims Act limits without expansion, and provides that temporary flooding is not a taking.

Section 5 continues the three management agreements and permits in force during the interim period ending the later of three years after enactment or the conveyance date; if no agreement is executed within three years, the Secretary manages the unconveyed land under applicable law.
